info.bio:
Cypress Hill es un grupo de hip hop proveniente de South Gate, California. Fue formado en 1986 y a lo largo de su amplia y exitosa carrera han vendido más de 46 millones de álbumes en todo el mundo.

El grupo está conformado por DJ Muggs (Lawrence Muggerud, DJ y productor, 28 de enero de 1968), B-Real (Louis Freese, Mc, 2 de junio de 1970), Sen Dog (Senen Reyes, Mc, 20 de noviembre de 1965) y Eric Bobo (Eric Correa, percusionista, 27 de agosto de 1968, que se integró en 1994).

scenes.name: DJ Quik, MC Eiht y Cypress Hill
scenes.book: The Come Up: An Oral History of the Rise of Hip-Hop
scenes.author: Jonathan Abrams
scenes.desc: Fuera de Death Row, DJ Quik y MC Eiht, a menudo rivales, retrataron Compton: Quik, que aprendió sampleando «Computer Love» en la caja de ritmos que Kelvin Anderson compró a Sir Jinx, fue un productor de G-funk muy musical, «al nivel de Rakim» para los angelinos. Cypress Hill (Sen Dog, B-Real y DJ Muggs), de South Gate, unieron inglés y castellano, Compton y East L.A., y la marihuana sin complejos; su primer disco (Ruffhouse, 1991) tenía temática del Oeste y bases del Este, con «The Phuncky Feel One» / «How I Could Just Kill a Man».
scenes.family: Costa Oeste: Los Ángeles, Compton, la Bahía

scenes.name: Rap y hip hop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: A finales de los ochenta el «rockero» es una figura tan obsoleta como lo fue el cantante pop en 1956: tres revoluciones toman la música popular (el DJ como fuerza creativa, el hip hop y la fusión ciberpunk de industrial, metal y hardcore). En 1975 Kool Herc reinventa el breakbeat en el Bronx; el rap es una evolución del dub jamaicano. Sugar Hill Gang, Kurtis Blow, los «mensajes» de Grandmaster Flash, Afrika Bambaataa (el Leonardo del beatbox, inventor del «electro»), el tocadiscos como instrumento, Run-DMC, Tackhead, L.L. Cool J, Eric B & Rakim y Public Enemy (It Takes A Nation Of Millions, la obra maestra del hip hop). El gangsta rap (Schoolly D, NWA, Ice Cube, Dr Dre, 2Pac), Beastie Boys, las raperas (MC Lyte, Queen Latifah), De La Soul, A Tribe Called Quest, Cypress Hill; en Gran Bretaña, Art Of Noise.
scenes.family: Soul, funk, disco, hip hop y baile

scenes.desc: The RZA, con su proyecto paralelo Gravediggaz, inventa el horrorcore —en paralelo a Cypress Hill—, mucho clavicordio y violines; una variante que generó incontables clones.

podcast.title: Lollapalooza 1991 Performer
podcast.body: Cypress Hill was among the "rap stars" who performed at the 1991 Lollapalooza festival, playing a key role in the event's groundbreaking integration of alternative rock and hardcore rap, which helped to bridge racial and social barriers. "When presented with rap stars like Ice Tea and Ice Cube at a tribe called Quest in George Clinton and Cypress Hill."

podcast.title: Judgment Night Collaboration with Pearl Jam (1993)
podcast.body: Cypress Hill collaborated with rock band Pearl Jam for the 1993 *Judgment Night* soundtrack. This pairing was considered radical at the time due to the limited crossover between rock and hip-hop. The project was a major catalyst for the creation of rap rock and nu metal, and helped bridge the divide between rock and hip-hop fans. "The pairings included Pearl Jam and Cypress Hill, Slayer working with Ice Tea, Faith No More and Buella Tribe, Dinosaur Jr., and Del the Funky Homo sapien, 11 collaborations at all."

podcast.title: Shared Combatant Spirit
podcast.body: Along with System of a Down, Cypress Hill adopted a combatant spirit directed against the system, moving beyond purely personal feelings to address broader societal issues. This ideological alignment mirrored the protest-oriented music of groups like Rage Against the Machine, demonstrating a continued thread of resistance within rock. "Cómo sistema fadda aún, o cómo los Cypress Hill también retomaban ese espíritu combatiente en contra del sistema inotanto, en contra del sentimiento personal."

xref.title: Audioslave Formed After Rick Rubin Suggested Chris Cornell; Be Real of Cypress Hill Also Auditioned
xref.body: After Zack de la Rocha quit Rage Against the Machine in 2000, the remaining three members tried to continue under the RATM name with a new singer. Be Real of Cypress Hill auditioned. But after some jamming, they decided they didn't want a Zack sound-alike — they wanted something new. Producer Rick Rubin suggested they talk to ex-Soundgarden singer Chris Cornell. The chemistry was immediate. They began writing as "Civilian" or "the Civilian project" but had to rename when they discovered another group was using that name. They chose Audioslave. The group was essentially Rage with a different singer, and they were productive from 2001 through 2007. "The chemistry was immediate."

xref.title: Travis Barker's Clothing Company – Famous Stars and Straps
xref.body: Travis Barker, drummer for blink-182, founded the clothing company Famous Stars and Straps in 1999, based in Corona, California. The brand targets the skate crowd and offers t-shirts, jackets, and hats for men, along with shirts, pants, and bikinis for women, in addition to accessories like belt buckles and bandanas. The company's success is bolstered by famous friends, including Tim Armstrong of Rancid, Steve-O of Sum 41, members of Avenged Sevenfold, and B-Real of Cypress Hill, who wear the brand publicly. Famous Stars and Straps generates millions in annual revenue, and its presence is notable at events like the Warped Tour. "He founded the company in 1999 and targeted the Skate Crowd."
